description: Check whether a team has an answer to one threat. For each team member it calculates the threat's hardest hit into it, its hardest hit into the threat, and who moves first, then gives a verdict. Counter: takes under 50% from the threat's hardest hit, so it survives two, and KOs the threat in 2 hits or fewer. Check: KOs the threat before it can KO back, needing fewer hits than the threat, or as many while moving first. Trade: each needs the same number of hits, so Speed decides (or a Speed tie leaves it open). Loses: anything else. A KO in N hits counts only when the damage rolls make it at least 50% likely, ignoring accuracy; when recovery or chip damage is in play (Leftovers, weather, status), the calculator's own KO chance must reach that. Verdicts are given for normal Speed order and for Trick Room. If no team member is a Counter or Check, or no team is given, it suggests Counters and Checks from the 40 most used Pokémon in the regulation. Missing set details come from usage statistics. These are single hits with no partner, screens or stat changes; Intimidate, Fake Out and move priority are not counted. This is not a battle simulation.

format.description: Regulation id from list_formats. Defaults to "champions-regmc" (Pokémon Champions — Regulation M-C).

limit.description: Maximum entries to return (1–10). Defaults to 5

suggest.description: Search usage when the team has no answer; default true

ability.description: Ability. Defaults to the Pokémon's most used ability in the regulation.

item.description: Held item, or "none". Defaults to the Pokémon's most used item in the regulation.

moves.description: Moves; defaults to the most used attacks. Fake Out is excluded.

nature.description: Nature, such as Adamant or Timid. If nature and statPoints are both left out, the Pokémon's most common spread in the regulation's usage statistics is used.

pokemon.description: Pokémon name in English. Mega Evolutions are tracked separately, e.g. "Charizard-Mega-Y"

statPoints.description: Pokémon Champions stat points per stat (0–32 each, 66 in total). Stats left out get 0.
